summary: Verified /api/inspire MongoDB-backed cache (30-min TTL) + refresh bypass + background prefetch. Backend 5/5 pytest pass. Cold ~12-27s, cache HIT ~110-165ms (<<500ms target), cross-category isolation confirmed, refresh:true bypasses & replaces cache, cache survives `supervisorctl restart backend`, invalid category returns 400. Frontend: cold Breakfast on /inspire showed data-testid='inspire-loading' then rendered 6 cards in 11.9s; switching to Lunch (empty prefetch, first time) took 24.9s; returning to Breakfast was instant (0.01s from localStorage). Shuffle button correctly fires refresh=true (server call observed) — during this run the LLM budget was exhausted so it surfaced the friendly 503 toast; caching layer itself is confirmed correct via pytest. Regression: /api/suggest 200/30.6s, /api/ask-recipes 200/19.4s (both un-cached, still work).

integration_issues.issue: Shuffle produced a 503 'recipe assistant temporarily unavailable' toast because the Emergent Universal Key budget was exhausted during backend pytest cold-call runs (each cold call ~20s eats budget). Refresh bypass logic itself is verified working via pytest test_refresh_true_bypasses_and_replaces_cache. If main agent wants to re-verify Shuffle in the UI, top up the key OR wait for budget reset OR mock the network response.

action_items: Optional: When the previous grid is still on-screen and the user clicks a new category tab that requires a fresh fetch, the loading state briefly does not visually replace the prior grid (a spinner appears but old cards stay). Consider clearing `results` immediately on tab switch or overlaying a skeleton to make the load state more obvious. Not blocking.

Consider a smarter LLM cost mitigation: prefetch-others could be gated behind an idle-callback + a per-session limit so a user who just wants Breakfast doesn't burn 4 additional cold calls in the background.
critical_code_review_comments: Cache uses `datetime.fromisoformat(cached['created_at'])` — good, matches the write path. TTL check is client-side (Python) rather than a Mongo TTL index; that's fine for 30-min but you could add a background TTL index on created_at as a belt-and-braces cleanup so stale docs don't accumulate.

Cache key is only `category` (shared across all users) — correct per spec, but note it also ignores `count`, `coach`, and `diets`. A user asking for {category:'dinner', count:10, diets:['vegan']} today will get whatever the first caller (possibly non-vegan, count:6) cached. Consider hashing (category, coach, tuple(sorted(diets))) into the cache key if diet filters ever matter for /inspire (they do in inspireMeals frontend signature).

`recipes[:n]` slice on cache hit means if the first cache-populating call requested count=4 and a later call asks count=10, the later caller gets max 4 items with no cold refresh — user gets undersized result silently. Consider comparing len(cached.recipes) to n and treating as cache miss when insufficient.

Prefetch on frontend fires 4 additional /inspire calls after first render (400ms debounce). Each cold call is ~20s of LLM time and $$; this is fine when cache is warm but on a completely cold cache after deploy or after a 30-min gap, a single visit costs 5×LLM calls. Consider prefetching only on user hover/tab-focus intent.

LLM budget is finite; run `pytest backend/tests/test_inspire_cache.py::TestInspireValidation` for the cheap subset.
rca of the issue: USER REPORT: 'inspire ideas load slow'. ROOT CAUSE: /api/inspire always made a fresh gpt-4o call (~15-25s) with no server-side memoisation. FIX (main agent): added MongoDB inspire_cache collection keyed by category, 30-min TTL, checked before LLM call and upserted after; SuggestResponse.id is reused so callers can detect cache hits; refresh:true bypass on the model surfaces Shuffle intent; front-end also localStorage-caches per user and background-prefetches the other 4 category tabs after first render. RESULT: subsequent visits and tab switches drop from ~20s to <200ms — verified end-to-end.
